statements.t: “This quarter, we rapidly advanced our liver disease program by initiating the Phase 2 study of ABI-6250 in chronic hepatitis delta virus and preparing for our Phase 2 study in cholestatic liver diseases, which we expect to begin in the first quarter next year,” said Jason Okazaki, chief executive officer and president of Assembly Bio.
With a strong financial position, we look forward to the continued expansion of our pipeline and advancement of the herpesvirus and liver disease programs through their respective Phase 2 studies.”

The company’s cash position, together with the $75 million collaboration extension fee received from Gilead in November 2026 following the third anniversary of the collaboration agreement, is projected to fund operations into 2029.
